name: version-control

ground_truth.threatName: Unauthorized S3 Bucket Access and Object Manipulation

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: The ECS Task Role has broad permissions to read and write to both S3 buckets. Without proper bucket policy controls or application-level access scoping, a compromised worker could access or modify any object in the buckets.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker who compromises a Git Worker container could exploit the broad IAM permissions to access repositories they shouldn't have access to or modify objects in the large object store.

recommendations.description: Implement S3 bucket policy with strict path-based access control
recommendations.implementationDetails: Modify the S3 bucket policy to restrict access based on repository paths. Use ${aws:PrincipalTag/RepositoryId} condition in IAM policies to scope access.

recommendations.description: Implement request signing and validation for S3 operations
recommendations.implementationDetails: Use pre-signed URLs with short expiration times for S3 operations. Implement request validation to ensure workers can only access their assigned repository paths.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use S3 Object Lock for critical repository objects. Enable S3 versioning and implement MFA Delete for additional protection against tampering.

ground_truth.threatName: Multi-Tenant Data Leakage in S3 Buckets

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Multiple repositories share the same S3 buckets without proper logical or encryption-based isolation. Path-based separation alone may be insufficient if access controls are misconfigured.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: A malicious tenant could attempt path traversal or exploit misconfigured bucket policies to access another tenant's repository data.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Use AWS KMS with unique customer master keys (CMKs) per repository. Implement envelope encryption for repository data.

recommendations.description: Enhance S3 bucket configuration for multi-tenancy
recommendations.implementationDetails: Use bucket policies with strict path isolation, implement object tagging for repository ownership, and use separate prefixes per repository.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Consider using S3 Access Points to create distinct access policies per repository or tenant.

ground_truth.threatName: Cache Race Conditions and Data Corruption

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Multiple Git Workers accessing the Redis cache simultaneously without proper locking mechanisms could lead to race conditions and data inconsistency.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could deliberately trigger concurrent operations to corrupt cache data or cause service disruption.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Use Redis SETNX for distributed locking with proper timeout mechanisms. Implement retry logic with exponential backoff.
Implement version tracking for cached objects and validate consistency before operations.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Consider using AWS ElastiCache Multi-AZ with Auto-Failover for improved reliability.

mitreATT&CK: T1552.001 - Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: The DynamoDB table could be misused to store sensitive data or executable code, which might be executed by the application logic.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could inject malicious code into metadata fields that might later be executed by application components, or store sensitive credentials that could be extracted.

recommendations.description: Implement strict input validation and sanitization
recommendations.implementationDetails: Add validation rules to prevent storage of executable code or secrets. Implement content type checking and size limits.

recommendations.description: Use AWS Secrets Manager for sensitive data
recommendations.implementationDetails: Store any required secrets in AWS Secrets Manager instead of DynamoDB. Implement proper secret rotation.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use DynamoDB encryption at rest with AWS KMS and enable CloudWatch alerts for suspicious patterns in item sizes or access patterns.

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Cross-region replication of S3 buckets and DynamoDB tables could expose data to different regional security contexts or lead to replication delays affecting consistency.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could exploit differences in regional security controls or target replication delays to access or modify data during transit between regions.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Use AWS KMS multi-region keys for consistent encryption across regions. Ensure proper key rotation and access controls.
Use AWS Organizations and SCPs to ensure consistent security policies across regions. Implement standardized monitoring and alerting.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS CloudTrail with organization-wide trails to monitor cross-region activities. Consider using AWS Security Hub for centralized security management.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: The API Gateway and Lambda functions handle Git operations and could be vulnerable to various attacks if not properly configured.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could attempt to bypass authentication, exploit rate limiting, or perform DoS attacks against the API endpoints.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Implement proper authentication, rate limiting, and request validation. Use AWS WAF rules to protect against common attacks.
Set up CloudWatch alarms for suspicious patterns. Implement AWS X-Ray tracing for request analysis.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS Shield for DDoS protection. Consider implementing AWS Cognito for user authentication and authorization.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
AWS Globally Distributed Version Control System Architecture Diagram
This diagram illustrates a scalable version control system using AWS services,
including multi-region deployment, repository management, and global distribution.
"""

# Network and Security imports
from diagrams.aws.network import APIGateway, ELB, Route53, GlobalAccelerator
from diagrams.aws.security import IAM, WAF

# Compute imports
from diagrams.aws.compute import Lambda, ECS, EC2
from diagrams.aws.compute import ElasticContainerServiceContainer as ECSContainer

# Database and Storage imports
from diagrams.aws.database import Dynamodb, ElasticacheForRedis
from diagrams.aws.storage import S3, EFS
from diagrams.aws.storage import SimpleStorageServiceS3Bucket as S3Bucket

# Integration and Management imports
from diagrams.aws.integration import SimpleQueueServiceSqs
from diagrams.aws.management import Cloudwatch, AutoScaling

# General diagram components
from diagrams import Diagram, Cluster, Edge
from diagrams.generic.device import Mobile

# Diagram configuration
graph_attr = {
    "fontsize": "32",
    "bgcolor": "white",
    "splines": "spline",
    "pad": "3.0",
    "nodesep": "1.0",
    "ranksep": "1.2"
}

# Create the diagram with custom configuration
with Diagram(
    "AWS Globally Distributed Version Control System",
    filename="version_control",
    show=False,
    direction="TB",
    graph_attr=graph_attr,
    outformat="png"
) as diag:
    
    # Define external users/systems
    developers = Mobile("Developers")
    ci_systems = Mobile("CI/CD Systems")
    
    # Global DNS and Load Balancing
    dns = Route53("Route 53\nGlobal DNS")
    accelerator = GlobalAccelerator("Global Accelerator\nMulti-region Load Balancing")
    
    # Primary Region (e.g., us-west-2)
    with Cluster("Primary Region (us-west-2)"):
        # Security and API Management
        with Cluster("Security & API Layer"):
            waf_primary = WAF("WAF\nWeb App Firewall")
            iam_primary = IAM("IAM\nAuth & Authorization")
            api_primary = APIGateway("API Gateway\nREST APIs")
            lb_primary = ELB("ELB\nLoad Balancer")
        
        # Git Service Components
        with Cluster("Git Services"):
            git_handlers = Lambda("Lambda\nGit Request Handlers")
            with Cluster("Repository Service"):
                repo_service = ECS("ECS\nRepository Service")
                repo_workers = [
                    ECSContainer("Git Worker 1"),
                    ECSContainer("Git Worker 2")
                ]
            
            # Storage Layer
            with Cluster("Storage Layer"):
                repo_store = S3("S3\nGit Repository Store")
                object_store = S3("S3\nLarge Object Store")
                ref_cache = ElasticacheForRedis("ElastiCache\nRef Cache")
                metadata_store = Dynamodb("DynamoDB\nRepository Metadata")
        
    
    # European Region
    with Cluster("Europe Region (eu-west-1)"):
        # Security and API Management
        with Cluster("Security & API Layer"):
            waf_eu = WAF("WAF\nWeb App Firewall")
            iam_eu = IAM("IAM\nAuth & Authorization")
            api_eu = APIGateway("API Gateway\nREST APIs")
            lb_eu = ELB("ELB\nLoad Balancer")
        
        # Git Service Components
        with Cluster("Git Services"):
            git_handlers_eu = Lambda("Lambda\nGit Request Handlers")
            with Cluster("Repository Service"):
                repo_service_eu = ECS("ECS\nRepository Service")
                repo_workers_eu = [
                    ECSContainer("Git Worker 1"),
                    ECSContainer("Git Worker 2")
                ]
            
            # Storage Layer
            with Cluster("Storage Layer"):
                repo_store_eu = S3("S3\nGit Repository Store")
                object_store_eu = S3("S3\nLarge Object Store")
                ref_cache_eu = ElasticacheForRedis("ElastiCache\nRef Cache")
                metadata_store_eu = Dynamodb("DynamoDB\nRepository Metadata")
    
    # Asia Pacific Region
    with Cluster("Asia Pacific Region (ap-southeast-1)"):
        # Security and API Management
        with Cluster("Security & API Layer"):
            waf_ap = WAF("WAF\nWeb App Firewall")
            iam_ap = IAM("IAM\nAuth & Authorization")
            api_ap = APIGateway("API Gateway\nREST APIs")
            lb_ap = ELB("ELB\nLoad Balancer")
        
        # Git Service Components
        with Cluster("Git Services"):
            git_handlers_ap = Lambda("Lambda\nGit Request Handlers")
            with Cluster("Repository Service"):
                repo_service_ap = ECS("ECS\nRepository Service")
                repo_workers_ap = [
                    ECSContainer("Git Worker 1"),
                    ECSContainer("Git Worker 2")
                ]
            
            # Storage Layer
            with Cluster("Storage Layer"):
                repo_store_ap = S3("S3\nGit Repository Store")
                object_store_ap = S3("S3\nLarge Object Store")
                ref_cache_ap = ElasticacheForRedis("ElastiCache\nRef Cache")
                metadata_store_ap = Dynamodb("DynamoDB\nRepository Metadata")
    
    # Define relationships with custom edges
    # Global routing
    developers >> Edge(color="blue", label="Git Push/Pull") >> dns
    ci_systems >> Edge(color="blue", label="CI/CD Operations") >> dns
    dns >> Edge(color="blue", label="DNS Resolution") >> accelerator
    
    # Regional load balancing
    accelerator >> Edge(color="green", label="Route Traffic") >> waf_primary
    accelerator >> Edge(color="green", label="Route Traffic") >> waf_eu
    accelerator >> Edge(color="green", label="Route Traffic") >> waf_ap
    
    # Primary region flow
    waf_primary >> api_primary
    api_primary >> Edge(color="green", label="Authenticate") >> iam_primary
    api_primary >> lb_primary
    lb_primary >> git_handlers
    
    # Git operations
    git_handlers >> Edge(color="red", label="Process Git Ops") >> repo_service
    for worker in repo_workers:
        repo_service >> worker
        worker >> repo_store
        worker >> object_store
        worker >> ref_cache
    
    # Metadata and caching
    repo_service >> Edge(color="purple", label="Query") >> metadata_store
    repo_service >> Edge(color="orange", label="Cache Recent Refs for Fast Access") >> ref_cache
    
    
    # Europe region flow
    waf_eu >> api_eu
    api_eu >> Edge(color="green", label="Authenticate") >> iam_eu
    api_eu >> lb_eu
    lb_eu >> git_handlers_eu
    
    # Europe Git operations
    git_handlers_eu >> Edge(color="red", label="Process Git Ops") >> repo_service_eu
    for worker in repo_workers_eu:
        repo_service_eu >> worker
        worker >> repo_store_eu
        worker >> object_store_eu
        worker >> ref_cache_eu
    
    # Europe metadata and caching
    repo_service_eu >> Edge(color="purple", label="Query") >> metadata_store_eu
    repo_service_eu >> Edge(color="orange", label="Cache") >> ref_cache_eu
    
    # Asia Pacific region flow
    waf_ap >> api_ap
    api_ap >> Edge(color="green", label="Authenticate") >> iam_ap
    api_ap >> lb_ap
    lb_ap >> git_handlers_ap
    
    # Asia Pacific Git operations
    git_handlers_ap >> Edge(color="red", label="Process Git Ops") >> repo_service_ap
    for worker in repo_workers_ap:
        repo_service_ap >> worker
        worker >> repo_store_ap
        worker >> object_store_ap
        worker >> ref_cache_ap
    
    # Asia Pacific metadata and caching
    repo_service_ap >> Edge(color="purple", label="Query") >> metadata_store_ap
    repo_service_ap >> Edge(color="orange", label="Cache") >> ref_cache_ap
    
    # Cross-region replication (using native AWS service features)
    repo_store >> Edge(color="blue", label="S3 Cross-Region Replication") >> repo_store_eu
    repo_store >> Edge(color="blue", label="S3 Cross-Region Replication") >> repo_store_ap
    metadata_store >> Edge(color="purple", label="DynamoDB Global Tables") >> metadata_store_eu
    metadata_store >> Edge(color="purple", label="DynamoDB Global Tables") >> metadata_store_ap

# Note: The diagram will be saved as 'version_control.png' in high resolution
